cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seat everyone. Why is the cake on the last spare chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The table wobbles. I put the last guest on the piano stool.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give the pianist my chair. You can move the cake to the table while I fix the leg.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake will fall if I put it there before you've fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand it to me, then. You fix the leg; I'm standing anyway now the pianist has my chair.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 runs seating; A3 gives up own chair and proposes moving cake; A5 swaps repair for holding it after B correction, accepting the burden produced by the whole chain.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 explains cake on spare chair and guest on stool; A3 moves pianist to A chair; B4 unsafe table timing causes A5 standing with cake while B fixes it.

relationship.evidence: B4 protects cake through a concrete sequencing correction, plausibly contributing to the solution.

heightening.evidence: A5 A standing with cake is earned by the earlier cake-occupied chair, displaced pianist and unrepaired table returning together.

specificity.evidence: B2 names guest and table problem; A3 gives the pianist A chair; no window or hidden spare seat is needed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 actual reassignment and reminder why A is standing replace an abstract everything-connected summary.
